exposure: US-guided conservative management of breast abscess (oral antibiotic treatment and needle aspiration)
microbiologic characterization of abscess material and milk samples
outcome: success of conservative breast abscess management (avoidance of incision and drainage)
microbiological profile of breast abscesses (including MRSA identification)
continuation of breastfeeding at 6 months and 3 months
cohort: 64 breastfeeding mothers diagnosed with breast abscess, with most developing the abscess within the first 100 days postpartum.
finding: A conservative, US-guided approach involving targeted antibiotic therapy (especially for MRSA) and needle aspiration was effective in managing breast abscesses of varying sizes in breastfeeding mothers, with none requiring incision and drainage and a significant proportion continuing breastfeeding for more than 6 months.
followup_time: up to 9.5 months post-delivery for breastfeeding duration
